extraction.name: PIQA
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning, where a model must choose the most sensible solution to a physical goal expressed in natural language. It targets everyday situations and physical knowledge about object properties, affordances, and manipulation.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Annotators were prompted with links to instructables and asked to glance at the instructions, then construct two component tasks by articulating a physical goal and a valid solution, and also provide a permutation of their own solution that makes it invalid. The dataset was further cleaned using AFLite to remove basic artifacts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Instructables.com instructions were used as the source/scaffold for annotation; the website is described as a crowdsourced collection of instructions for doing everything from cooking to car repair, often with images or videos and lists of tools.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were prompted with links to Instructables and asked to glance at the instructions, then construct two component tasks by articulating a physical goal and a valid solution; they were also asked to provide a permutation of their own solution that makes it invalid, often subtly.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper analyzes dataset difficulty via edit distance between solution choices and reports validation/training distributions and RoBERTa accuracy over examples with different edit distances and single-word replacements, but does not report inter-annotator agreement or formal annotation QC metrics.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 solution choices per item (one correct and one incorrect)
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset was designed to reduce reporting bias and flatten the distribution of referenced objects, since annotators initially favored prototypical kitchen/garage tools. It also uses instructables prompts to encourage atypical materials and out-of-the-box solutions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is focused on physical commonsense in everyday situations and may not generalize beyond that domain. The paper notes that physical commonsense is harder to pin down than syntax, and that many examples are small edits between solutions, which can still confuse models.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper frames PIQA as a benchmark to advance AI systems that understand physical commonsense, with potential relevance to robots and real-world interaction. It also aims to elicit further research into language representations that capture details of the real world.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for benchmarking and evaluation of physical commonsense understanding in multiple-choice question answering. It is used to evaluate language representations and model performance, including training/validation/testing splits for benchmarking.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: They prompted annotators with links to Instructables, asked them to construct two component tasks from an instructable, and asked for a permutation of their own solution that makes it invalid; this was done to flatten the distribution of referenced objects and assist diversity.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: They used state-of-the-art approaches for handling spurious biases and prompted annotators using Instructables to inspire goals and solutions.

inLanguage.evidence: Questions requiring this kind of physical commonsense pose a challenge to today’s natural language understanding systems.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: “we prompt the annotations with links to instructables... annotators were asked...”

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: “we provide a prompt to the annotators derived from instructables.com. The instructables website is a crowdsourced collection of instructions for doing everything from cooking to car repair. In most cases, users provide images or videos detailing each step and a list of tools that will be required.”

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: annotators were asked to glance at the instructions of an instructable and pull out or have it inspire them to construct two component tasks. rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We compute edit distance over tokenized and lowercased strings with punctuation removed. ... In the bottom of Figure 6, we show that the dataset complexity generally increases with the edit distance between the solution pairs.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: given a question q and two possible solutions s1, s2, a model or a human must choose the most appropriate solution, of which exactly one is correct

rai:dataBiases.evidence: “we use state-of-the-art approaches for handling spurious biases” and “reporting bias swamped the dataset” and “To address this, and flatten the distribution of referenced objects, we prompt the annotations with links to instructables.”

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: “physical commonsense does not have as rich a literature to borrow from, making its dimensions challenging to pin down” and “The majority of the dataset consists of small tweaks between the two solution pairs; nevertheless, this is enough to confuse state-of-the-art NLP models.”

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: “modeling physical commonsense knowledge is a major challenge on the road to true AI-completeness, including robots that interact with the world and understand natural language” and “our goal is to elicit further research into building language representations that capture details of the real world.”

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: “We introduce a new dataset, PIQA, for benchmarking progress in physical commonsense understanding” and “The underlying task is multiple choice question answering” and “Split Validation Training”
